Fractal Optimization of Tensor Landscapes

Training a network is a walk on a landscape. Where is that landscape fractal, and can the structure be turned into speed?

iori1

1Jorik Jonathan Chase, 3DIE — Design, Art & Technologies Label. Paper 2 of a series. In preparation.

Abstract

In preparation. Chapter 6 of paper 0 made precise. Two things are measured fractal today. The boundary between training that converges and training that diverges is fractal in the plane of learning rates, with box dimensions from 1.17 to 1.98 (Sohl-Dickstein 2024). The paths of stochastic gradient descent are self-affine, with path dimensions between 1.3 and 2.7 (Gong et al.). Under four stated assumptions SGD behaves like a walker at a temperature set by learning rate over batch size (Mandt, Hoffman and Blei 2017).

Every fast numerical method buys its speed with one regularity across scales: the FFT, multigrid, the fast multipole method, hierarchical matrices, Monarch layers. This paper asks whether trained networks have such a regularity, measures it, and does not claim what no source supports: recursion does not make an arbitrary shape or an arbitrary optimisation faster.

Planned contents

  1. What is measured fractal. The trainability boundary, SGD trajectories, the bulk and outliers of the Hessian spectrum, the edge of stability.
  2. SGD as a walker at a temperature. Where the Langevin picture holds, where its assumptions fail, and learning-rate schedules as annealing.
  3. Scale separation as speed. FFT, multigrid, fast multipole, H-matrices, butterfly and Monarch layers, each with the regularity it needs.
  4. The measurement. Do the weights of trained networks have low-rank far blocks or a power-law spectrum a fast method can use?
  5. Live figures. The walker of paper 0 in many dimensions; a fractal trainability boundary you can zoom.

What already exists

  • Paper 0, chapter 6: Barnes–Hut on Lévy dust and the table of fast methods.
  • Paper 0, section 4.2: a Metropolis walker on a fractal landscape.
  • Petri: a multigrid pressure solver in WebGPU.
